entities.name: Propriospinal relay neurons
entities.injuryContext: Spatially and temporally separated lateral hemisections
entities.allowedClaim: Propriospinal relay connections can mediate supraspinal control of stepping in the staggered-hemisection mouse model.
entities.notEstablished: Recovery across one anatomically complete lesion or a single molecular interneuron type.
negativeFindings: Retrograde brainstem labeling remained markedly reduced.
The model is not one anatomically complete lesion at a single level.

entities.name: dI3 glutamatergic interneurons
entities.injuryContext: Lower thoracic complete transection with treadmill training
entities.allowedClaim: dI3 glutamatergic output is necessary for stable locomotor recovery under the defined transection and training conditions.
entities.notEstablished: Activation of dI3 alone is sufficient, or an equivalent role in humans.
negativeFindings: Pre-injury fundamental rhythm and interlimb coordination were largely intact after output removal.
The study does not establish sufficiency.

entities.name: SC^Vsx2::Hoxa10
entities.injuryContext: Mouse SCI recovery and EES-assisted rehabilitation paradigms
entities.allowedClaim: Mouse experiments identified SC^Vsx2::Hoxa10 neurons as necessary and sufficient under defined recovery conditions.
entities.notEstablished: That the same population is the causal substrate of recovery in human EES participants.
negativeFindings: The human cohort was not a randomized comparison.
Mouse cell-type causality and human treatment outcomes are separate evidence streams.

entities.name: V3 interneurons
entities.allowedClaim: V3 interneurons are a necessary component of the sensory-driven sacral network that generates spasms under the test conditions.
entities.notEstablished: That V3 neurons are the sole generator of spasticity or that activation supports useful locomotion.
negativeFindings: This is a maladaptive spasm context, not a beneficial walking-recovery context.

entities.name: Ipsilateral cervical V2a neurons
entities.allowedClaim: Spared ipsilateral cervical V2a neurons can support diaphragm recruitment and become necessary for selected injured-state respiratory output.
entities.notEstablished: Durable recovery without stimulation, lumbar locomotor recovery, or clinical efficacy.
negativeFindings: This evidence concerns breathing, not walking.

entities.name: Vgat+/KCC2-sensitive state
entities.allowedClaim: KCC2 manipulation altered inhibitory-neuron excitability and enabled spared relay pathways in the defined mouse model.
entities.notEstablished: A general benefit of global disinhibition or efficacy after anatomically complete transection.
negativeFindings: CLP290 failed after complete T8 transection.
The intervention did not increase descending or propriospinal axon growth.
Residual antagonist-muscle coactivation indicated suboptimal coordination.

entities.name: vGlut2-lineage transmitter switching
entities.injuryContext: Neonatal and adult complete thoracic transection shown as separate conditions
entities.allowedClaim: Injury age and activity shape transmitter phenotype, and attenuating the adult inhibitory switch improved selected locomotor features.
entities.notEstablished: Complete recovery or a general benefit from suppressing inhibitory signaling.
negativeFindings: Adult vGAT attenuation produced variable, partial, poorly coordinated stepping.
Training alone did not significantly improve locomotor ability.
Neonatal and adult conditions must not be pooled.
